scope: Verification packets for all candidates retained after title-and-abstract screening. These records support curation decisions but are not curated graph sources or claims.

stage_definitions.full_text_checked: The accessible article full text was inspected for design, results, and limitations.
stage_definitions.publisher_page_checked: The official publisher article page and abstract were inspected; detailed full-text extraction is still required.
stage_definitions.doi_abstract_verified: DOI metadata and the indexed abstract were checked; detailed full-text extraction is still required.

recommendation_definitions.ready_for_structured_curation: The paper can proceed to source-profile and atomic-claim drafting, followed by locator-level checking.
recommendation_definitions.hold_for_full_text_extraction: Retain the paper, but do not promote it into the curated graph until the full text is extracted.

records.study_type: Remote-sensing method and land-cover time series
records.spatial_scope: Three ecoregions across the Seward and Tuktoyaktuk peninsulas, approximately 335,000 square kilometres
records.temporal_scope: Annual mapping from 2016 through 2023
methods: Landsat and Sentinel-2 optical remote sensing
records.headline_result: Produced annual fractional land-cover and change maps intended to resolve heterogeneous Arctic tundra more effectively than categorical products.
principal_limitations: Validation is regional rather than pan-Arctic.
Change-detection performance is weaker than static cover estimation.
Full-text checking is needed before quoting class-specific accuracy or trend values.

records.study_type: Lake-succession field study and food-web biogeochemistry
records.spatial_scope: A glacier-retreat chronosequence of lakes in southern Greenland
records.temporal_scope: Contemporary sampling across lakes of different postglacial ages
methods: Compound-specific stable-isotope analysis of amino acids
Arctic char tissue and food-web sampling
records.headline_result: Links glacier retreat and lake succession to changing organic nutrient sources and reports that aquatic production supplies much of Arctic char long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids.
principal_limitations: A space-for-time chronosequence does not directly observe temporal change within a lake.
Dietary pathways and cannibalism are partly inferred from biochemical tracers.
Exact effect sizes and sampling replication require full-text extraction.

records.study_type: Zooplankton field survey and distribution projection
records.spatial_scope: Pacific Gateway sector of the Arctic Ocean
records.temporal_scope: Fifty-four net casts in summer 2024 with projections to 2100 under SSP2-4.5
records.headline_result: Projects habitat contraction for a multi-taxon soft-bodied zooplankton assemblage in the Pacific Gateway, treated as a regional Arctic bottleneck.
principal_limitations: The future result is modelled rather than directly observed.
Projection uncertainty depends on the environmental predictors and climate scenario.
A single-season survey may underrepresent interannual and seasonal variability.

records.spatial_scope: Two Arctic grassland sites in northern Fennoscandia
records.temporal_scope: Contemporary grazing-exclusion and nutrient-addition experiment
records.headline_result: Reports that grazing and nutrient enrichment reshape pollinator communities and interaction networks, with responses depending on their interaction and site context.
principal_limitations: Only two sites were studied.
Experimental duration may not represent long-term vegetation and pollinator adjustment.
Full text is required to distinguish abundance, diversity, and network-metric effects.

records.spatial_scope: Northern West Siberia, including ancient permafrost and contemporary soils
records.temporal_scope: Contemporary samples compared with approximately 10,000- and 39,000-year-old permafrost
methods: Assembly and binning of 117 metagenome-assembled genomes
records.headline_result: Provides genomes that contrast microbial diversity and inferred functional potential between ancient permafrost and modern northern soils.
principal_limitations: Genome annotations indicate potential, not measured activity.
MAG completeness and contamination constrain organism-level interpretation.
Antimicrobial-resistance and biosynthetic functions should not be equated with phenotype without validation.

records.spatial_scope: Middle- and Late-Pleistocene Siberian permafrost
records.temporal_scope: Ancient deposits compared through metagenomic sequence evidence
methods: Recovery of 2,697 viral operational taxonomic units
records.headline_result: Reports extensive viral diversity in Pleistocene permafrost and infers possible host associations and ecological functions.
principal_limitations: Recovered sequences do not demonstrate viral viability or contemporary activity.
Hosts and auxiliary metabolic genes are computational predictions.
Age and locality constrain generalization to present-day Arctic permafrost.

records.spatial_scope: Jonah's icefish, an Antarctic notothenioid fish
records.temporal_scope: Contemporary reference-genome resource
records.headline_result: Presents an approximately 1.27-gigabase, 24-chromosome assembly with reported high completeness and about 31,777 annotated genes.
principal_limitations: A reference assembly is an enabling resource, not direct evidence for a particular adaptation.
Gene annotations require functional confirmation.
Population variation cannot be inferred from one reference assembly.

records.spatial_scope: South Georgia seabird colony with comparison to Kerguelen data
records.temporal_scope: More than 250 chicks from eight species sampled during 2018-2020
records.headline_result: Finds strong interspecific mercury variation associated with trophic ecology across an albatross and petrel community.
principal_limitations: Chick feathers integrate a restricted life stage and time window.
Stable-isotope associations do not prove the causal source of mercury.
Cross-archipelago comparisons may be affected by year and method differences.

records.study_type: Comparative bulk sea-ice metagenomics and viral genome recovery
records.spatial_scope: Nine samples from sea ice north of Svalbard, the northern Baltic Sea, and the western and eastern Weddell Gyre
records.temporal_scope: Baltic winter 2006, Antarctic winter 2013, and Arctic early summer 2015
methods: Recovery and dereplication of 550 viral operational taxonomic units
records.headline_result: Recovers 550 vOTUs, predicts hosts for 187, and assigns functions to 56% of viral gene products, including candidate auxiliary functions across oxidative metabolism, photosynthesis, and stress regulation.
principal_limitations: The nine samples differ in year, season, region, layer pooling, and storage history.
Bulk membrane-filter metagenomes were not viral-particle enriched and most recovered viral genomes were incomplete.
Host, lifestyle, and auxiliary-function assignments are computational rather than direct infection or expression measurements.

records.spatial_scope: A Canadian High Arctic shoreline
records.temporal_scope: Thirty-three-day field mesocosm experiment
methods: In situ mesocosms with three ship fuels
records.headline_result: Demonstrates measurable microbial biodegradation of new-generation ship fuels under High Arctic shoreline conditions.
principal_limitations: One shoreline and a short mesocosm cannot represent an operational spill across Arctic seasons.
Treatment conditions simplify dilution, transport, weathering, and ecological interactions.
Fuel-specific percentages require full-text confirmation.

records.study_type: Cultivation and comparative genomics of extremotolerant bacteria
records.spatial_scope: Peary Land, extreme North Greenland
records.temporal_scope: Contemporary isolates from an Arctic terrestrial environment
records.headline_result: Describes novel halotolerant bacterial diversity and candidate genomic features associated with cold and salt tolerance.
principal_limitations: Cultivation selects a small, growable fraction of the community.
Only nine isolates received genome-level analysis.
Annotated adaptation genes do not alone demonstrate their ecological role in situ.

records.spatial_scope: Two viruses infecting the Arctic phytoplankter Micromonas polaris
records.temporal_scope: Laboratory infection dynamics with comparison to environmental metagenomes
records.headline_result: Characterizes two approximately 203-204-kilobase dsDNA viruses and investigates how their infection dynamics may allow coexistence on a shared Arctic host.
principal_limitations: Experiments use a cultured host-virus system under controlled conditions.
A single host strain cannot represent natural host diversity.
Environmental coexistence mechanisms remain inferential until validated in situ.

records.spatial_scope: Antarctic fur seals at King George Island
records.temporal_scope: Four contemporary faecal samples
records.headline_result: Describes taxonomic and functional features of the fur-seal gut microbiome, including chitin-related pathways and predicted pathogenicity or resistance markers.
principal_limitations: The sample size is only four animals.
Faecal metagenomes represent host-associated potential, not environmental prevalence or activity.
Predicted pathogens and resistance genes do not establish infection or phenotypic resistance.

records.spatial_scope: Greenland meltwater pathways and the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation
records.temporal_scope: SSP5-8.5 ensembles through 2300
methods: High-end Greenland meltwater forcing based on CESM2-CISM2
records.headline_result: In this model setup, Greenland meltwater adds about 1 sverdrup of AMOC weakening by 2100 and up to 4 sverdrups by 2300, without producing abrupt or centennially irreversible collapse.
principal_limitations: The result comes from one coupled climate model.
Meltwater pathway and freshwater-forcing implementation are model dependent.
The high-end forcing is not a probabilistic forecast, so the result should not be generalized as ruling out abrupt change.

records.spatial_scope: Southern Ocean forcing and tropical atmospheric response
records.temporal_scope: Idealized and historical model experiments rather than a direct forecast
methods: Mean-state bias correction and teleconnection diagnostics
records.headline_result: Shows that a more realistic tropical mean state, especially the ITCZ and surface winds, strengthens simulated tropical responses to Southern Ocean cooling through wind-evaporation feedbacks.
principal_limitations: The mechanism is diagnosed within a limited model hierarchy.
Results depend on prescribed Southern Ocean perturbations and bias-correction choices.
Improved model agreement is not direct observational attribution of a historical event.

records.spatial_scope: Polar, brown, and black bear genomes
records.temporal_scope: Contemporary genome samples interpreted in an evolutionary comparison
methods: Whole-genome comparison of 10 brown, 13 polar, and 11 black bears
records.headline_result: Identifies lineage-dominant transposable-element insertions, especially CAN SINE events, concentrated near untranslated or regulatory regions rather than coding sequence; fixed derived insertions potentially affect regulation of 67 genes.
principal_limitations: Regulatory effects are predicted from genomic position and annotation, not demonstrated experimentally.
Sample sizes remain modest for population-level fixation claims.
Candidate links to Arctic adaptation require expression and functional validation.

records.study_type: Community-engaged coastal mapping and sea-level modelling
records.spatial_scope: Aasiaat and adjacent channels in western Greenland
records.temporal_scope: Local relative sea-level projections to 2100 under RCP2.6 and RCP8.5
methods: Community knowledge and collaborative research design
records.headline_result: Projects a local relative sea-level fall of approximately 0.41-0.93 metres by 2100, with potential shoaling or closure of navigation channels and consequences for water exchange and ecosystems.
principal_limitations: Local projections depend on ice-mass and glacial-isostatic-adjustment scenarios.
Threshold effects in shallow channels are sensitive to bathymetric and vertical-datum uncertainty.
Navigation and nutrient consequences are projected implications, not observations through 2100.

records.study_type: Narrative review of polar giant viruses
records.spatial_scope: Arctic and Antarctic environments
records.temporal_scope: Synthesis of published polar giant-virus observations
methods: Comparison of diversity, endemism, adaptation, and ecological structuring
records.headline_result: Synthesizes evidence that giant viruses are diverse components of polar ecosystems and discusses their biogeography, adaptation, and potential ecological roles.
principal_limitations: This is secondary synthesis rather than new primary measurements.
Conclusions inherit geographic, seasonal, cultivation, and annotation biases in the underlying literature.
Publisher-page inspection is not sufficient for section-level synthesis claims.

records.spatial_scope: Seventeen benthic mats from 15 Arctic, Antarctic, and sub-Antarctic lakes, from littoral sites to 6.5 metres depth
records.temporal_scope: Cross-sectional comparison of contemporary lake mats
methods: Read mapping and multivariate environmental analysis
records.headline_result: Finds a shared functional core involving stress responses and phosphorus cycling while identifying environmental and climate-associated differences among polar lake mats.
principal_limitations: Most lakes are represented by one sample, limiting within-lake replication.
Gene content is functional potential, not process rate or expression.
Uneven sites, depths, and environmental conditions complicate pole-level attribution.

records.spatial_scope: Circum-Antarctic sea ice with regional emphasis on the Weddell and Ross sectors
records.temporal_scope: 1979-2023, with an inferred interdecadal shift around 1998
records.headline_result: Reports that the spring Southern Annular Mode's lagged association with summer Antarctic sea ice strengthened after the late 1990s through a stronger PSA-like circulation and Amundsen Sea Low pathway.
principal_limitations: The shift and mechanisms are statistical and diagnostic rather than experimentally causal.
Results can depend on period selection and reanalysis or sea-ice products.
Regional pathways differ, so a circumpolar summary can hide opposing responses.

records.spatial_scope: Ornithogenic tundra soil in South Spitsbergen
records.temporal_scope: Contemporary bacterial isolates
methods: Physiological assays for denitrification, nitrogen fixation, and chemolithotrophy
records.headline_result: Describes two psychrophilic taxa in a new genus and reports distinct genomic or physiological capacities relevant to tundra nitrogen cycling.
principal_limitations: Evidence comes from two cultured strains at one site.
Laboratory physiology does not establish abundance or realized process rates in soil.
Community-level nitrogen-cycle importance remains untested.

records.spatial_scope: Bayelva active-layer soil near Ny-Alesund and fjord sediments in Van Keulenfjorden and Kongsfjorden, Svalbard
records.temporal_scope: Fjord samples from 2016 and active-layer cores from March 2021
methods: Recovery of 49 fjord and 44 active-layer MAGs
records.headline_result: Shows genetic capacity and multi-omic evidence for degradation of land-derived carbohydrates in both thawed active-layer soil and Arctic fjord sediments, indicating burial does not guarantee preservation.
principal_limitations: The study demonstrates capacity and molecular activity rather than a whole-fjord carbon flux.
Sites and sampling years differ between terrestrial and marine systems.
MAG-based functions and omic signals do not assign every process to a cultured organism.

records.spatial_scope: An 18-27-centimetre active-layer interval from Bayelva near Ny-Alesund, Svalbard
records.temporal_scope: One frozen core incubated at 4 degrees Celsius for 21 and 98 days
records.headline_result: Identifies early and late microbial growers after thaw and suggests growth, predation, and epibiosis structure community succession while carbon dioxide is rapidly produced.
principal_limitations: The experiment uses one core and laboratory incubation.
Incubation at constant temperature simplifies field freeze-thaw and hydrology.
Low net methane and isotope-labelled methane-oxidizer growth should not be interpreted as a landscape methane budget.

records.spatial_scope: Human-impacted wastewater, fjord, and ice-associated environments of Spitsbergen
records.temporal_scope: Contemporary cross-sectional sampling
records.headline_result: Profiles stress-response genes, resistance determinants, virulence-associated genes, and microbial populations along human-impact gradients in High Arctic environments.
principal_limitations: Gene detection does not demonstrate expression, transfer, pathogenicity, or health risk.
A cross-sectional snapshot cannot establish temporal persistence or source attribution.
Relative sequence abundance is not equivalent to viable-cell abundance.

records.study_type: In situ oil-exposure and degrader-identification experiment
records.spatial_scope: Faroe-Shetland Channel sub-Arctic water at approximately 500 metres depth
records.temporal_scope: Four-day in situ dialysis exposure
methods: In situ dialysis incubation with crude oil
records.headline_result: Characterizes a rapid sub-Arctic bacterioplankton response to crude oil and identifies candidate oil-degrading community members with complementary methods.
principal_limitations: The experiment is short and restricted to one sub-Arctic water mass and depth.
Enclosure and oil-addition conditions differ from plume transport in an actual spill.
Sub-Arctic findings should not be generalized across the central Arctic Ocean.

records.study_type: Wildlife disease detection, viral genomics, and movement ecology
records.spatial_scope: Gough Island in the South Atlantic, with genomic comparison to South Georgia and Antarctic or sub-Antarctic outbreaks
records.temporal_scope: Three great-skua carcasses from a reported 2024-2025 event, combined with tracking and regional viral genomes
records.headline_result: Confirms H5N1 in three great skuas on Gough Island and finds the sequenced viruses closely related to Antarctic and sub-Antarctic lineages, with tracking data supporting a plausible South Georgia connection.
principal_limitations: Only three birds were positive and two yielded near-complete viral genomes.
The incursion route is inferred from phylogeny and movement rather than directly observed transmission.
The full text contains an apparent inconsistency between the observation and collection years that must be resolved before citing the date.

records.study_type: Two-year multi-depth marine eDNA metabarcoding survey
records.spatial_scope: Ross Sea Region Marine Protected Area, with stations and CTD depths spanning distinct water masses
records.temporal_scope: Austral late-summer surveys in 2024 and 2025
records.headline_result: Detects 92 species in both survey years and associates vertical and horizontal eukaryotic community structure primarily with thermal stratification and water-mass properties.
principal_limitations: eDNA presence is not organism abundance, viability, or activity.
Both campaigns sampled late summer, leaving other seasons unresolved.
Marker choice, incomplete reference databases, and unequal station designs constrain completeness and direct year-to-year comparison.
